title: I Took the Vet Boarding Vaccine Log to the Desk That Waived It

parts.text: I dropped my dog at 8:05 a.m. with a current vaccine PDF. The desk waived a boarder's missing bordetella because they were a friend of the tech. The policy on the wall said no exceptions. I was thirty-seven, anxious about kennel cough in a room of exceptions. I asked them to log the waiver. They said they do not log friends. I photographed the wall, my PDF, and the unnamed friend dog on the intake screen. Then I emailed the vet-owner, not the desk. At 8:14 the friend dog was already in the playgroup with mine.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The friend dog is in playgroup while the wall still says no exceptions.

social.video_title: Wall policy, waived bordetella, playgroup anyway — Part 1/2
social.description: PDF in hand, unnamed friend, owner email. Would you have taken your dog back immediately?

parts.text: The owner pulled the friend for a shot or a go-home. They chose the shot. My dog stayed. The desk started logging waivers, which meant waivers died. Wall text matched intake. I picked up a dog that had played with equals. Friends can use the same needle. Exceptions are how coughs travel. I keep PDFs. The intake screen learned names. Playgroup is a policy, not a vibe.

social.description: Waivers logged to death, equals in playgroup. Was a friend a titer?
